INDIA Bloc Alleges Electoral Integrity Violations, Holds Public Impeachment Over CEC Gyanesh Kumar

01 Nov 2026, 10:42 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Sports Desk · Source: news.abplive.com

Overview

On Saturday, the Congress-led INDIA bloc held a symbolic 'public impeachment' session for Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. Framing its allegations as a fight to protect democratic integrity—a principle also central to fair play in competitive sports—the Opposition used the event to highlight perceived threats to India's electoral processes.

The proceedings, presided over by former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar, were structured to resemble a functioning parliamentary session. The seating arrangement and a stage with a backdrop modelled on the old Central Hall of Parliament were designed to mimic traditional legislative settings. The event was streamed live on X through Rahul Gandhi's account and other party handles.

Key Allegations

The INDIA bloc's motion against CEC Gyanesh Kumar lists six specific charges, alleging serious violations of democratic processes akin to integrity violations in competitive environments:

  • Conspiring to steal elections.
  • Deleting 13.2 crore (132 million) voters from electoral rolls.
  • Rewriting Form 6, used for voter enrolment, without Parliament's approval.
  • Taking control of voter rolls through ECINET, the Election Commission's online system.
  • Excluding the other two Election Commissioners from the process.
  • Acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah.

Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar opened the proceedings, stating that improper removal of voters and lack of transparency in the Election Commission's responses necessitated the impeachment motion. She emphasized India's position as the world's largest democracy, noting that other nations look to its model.

Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge moved the symbolic motion, arguing that the right to vote is under serious threat. He accused the ruling establishment of using various means to retain power, including breaking political parties, toppling governments, electoral bonds, and central investigative agencies like the ED and CBI.

BJP Counter-Narrative

The BJP swiftly responded, with spokesperson Guru Prakash Paswan describing the event as a 'mockery, not a mock parliament.' The party took a swipe at Rahul Gandhi, stating he was now 'sitting in a Parliament of his own choice, unable to win elections in reality.'

Union Home Minister Amit Shah previously challenged Rahul Gandhi and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav to debate electoral rolls in a special session of Parliament, asserting the BJP was prepared to discuss the matter and had nothing to hide.

Practical Implications and Verification

The Opposition has been demanding Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, the suspension of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, and the restoration of pre-revision electoral rolls. The SIR exercise has resulted in the deletion of approximately 14% of the pre-SIR voter count.

This issue has previously led to repeated disruptions in Parliament. During the 2025 monsoon session, little business was transacted apart from discussions on Operation Sindoor, with frequent adjournments largely over the SIR exercise in Bihar. In the winter session, the government agreed to a discussion on electoral reforms instead of a debate specifically on the SIR.

To verify this announcement, readers can refer to the original report published by ABP Live at the provided source URL. The source text indicates that the mock proceedings were initially scheduled for Friday but were postponed by a day because of rain in Delhi.
